Find the radius of convergence of the power series ∑n=0∞n2+13n xn\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{n^2+1}{3^n}\,x^n∑n=0∞​3nn2+1​xn.

∣cn+1xn+1cnxn∣=(n+1)2+1n2+1⋅∣x∣3→∣x∣3\left|\frac{c_{n+1}x^{n+1}}{c_n x^n}\right| = \frac{(n+1)^2+1}{n^2+1}\cdot\frac{|x|}{3} \to \frac{|x|}{3}​cn​xncn+1​xn+1​​=n2+1(n+1)2+1​⋅3∣x∣​→3∣x∣​
  • Power Series and Radius of Convergence
Show solution

  1. With cn=n2+13n>0c_n = \frac{n^2+1}{3^n} > 0cn​=3nn2+1​>0, the ratio of successive absolute terms is ∣cn+1xn+1cnxn∣=(n+1)2+1n2+1⋅∣x∣3\left|\frac{c_{n+1}x^{n+1}}{c_n x^n}\right| = \frac{(n+1)^2+1}{n^2+1}\cdot\frac{|x|}{3}​cn​xncn+1​xn+1​​=n2+1(n+1)2+1​⋅3∣x∣​.

  2. Since (n+1)2+1n2+1=n2+2n+2n2+1→1\frac{(n+1)^2+1}{n^2+1} = \frac{n^2+2n+2}{n^2+1} \to 1n2+1(n+1)2+1​=n2+1n2+2n+2​→1, the ratio tends to ∣x∣3\frac{|x|}{3}3∣x∣​.

  3. By the ratio test the series converges (absolutely) for ∣x∣<3|x| < 3∣x∣<3, and for ∣x∣>3|x| > 3∣x∣>3 the general term ∣cnxn∣=(n2+1)(∣x∣3)n→∞\left|c_n x^n\right| = (n^2+1)\left(\frac{|x|}{3}\right)^n \to \infty∣cn​xn∣=(n2+1)(3∣x∣​)n→∞, so it diverges. Hence the radius of convergence is R=3R = 3R=3.

2Medium

Prove that ∑n=1∞n(−1)n\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n(-1)^n∑n=1∞​n(−1)n diverges in the ordinary sense but is Abel summable, with Abel sum −14-\frac{1}{4}−41​.

∑n≥1n(−1)nxn=−x(1+x)2→x→1−−14\sum_{n\ge 1} n(-1)^n x^n = -\frac{x}{(1+x)^2} \xrightarrow[x\to 1^{-}]{} -\frac{1}{4}n≥1∑​n(−1)nxn=−(1+x)2x​x→1−​−41​
  • Abel's Theorem
Show solution

  1. Divergence first: the general term n(−1)nn(-1)^nn(−1)n does not tend to 000 (since ∣n(−1)n∣=n→∞|n(-1)^n| = n \to \infty∣n(−1)n∣=n→∞), so the series diverges by the nnn-th term test.

  2. For ∣z∣<1|z| < 1∣z∣<1, differentiating ∑n=0∞zn=11−z\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} z^n = \frac{1}{1-z}∑n=0∞​zn=1−z1​ termwise (a power series may be differentiated termwise inside its disc) gives ∑n=1∞nzn−1=1(1−z)2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n z^{n-1} = \frac{1}{(1-z)^2}∑n=1∞​nzn−1=(1−z)21​; multiplying by zzz yields the formula below.

    ∑n=1∞nzn=z(1−z)2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n z^n = \frac{z}{(1-z)^2}n=1∑∞​nzn=(1−z)2z​

  3. Substituting z=−xz = -xz=−x (0≤x<10 \le x < 10≤x<1) gives n(−x)n=n(−1)nxnn(-x)^n = n(-1)^n x^nn(−x)n=n(−1)nxn, so ∑n=1∞n(−1)nxn=−x(1+x)2\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n(-1)^n x^n = \frac{-x}{(1+x)^2}∑n=1∞​n(−1)nxn=(1+x)2−x​. As x→1−x \to 1^{-}x→1− this tends to −14-\frac{1}{4}−41​, the Abel sum.

    A divergent series can still be Abel summable.

3Medium

Prove rigorously that the rearrangement of the alternating harmonic series taking "two positive terms, then one negative term" in order, 1+13−12+15+17−14+⋯1+\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{7}-\frac{1}{4}+\cdots1+31​−21​+51​+71​−41​+⋯, converges to 32ln⁡2\frac{3}{2}\ln 223​ln2.

(You may use Hm=ln⁡m+γ+o(1)H_m = \ln m+\gamma+o(1)Hm​=lnm+γ+o(1) as known.)

T3N=H4N−12H2N−12HN→32ln⁡2T_{3N} = H_{4N}-\tfrac12 H_{2N}-\tfrac12 H_N \to \tfrac32\ln 2T3N​=H4N​−21​H2N​−21​HN​→23​ln2
  • Rearranging Changes the Sum
  • Riemann's Rearrangement Theorem
Show solution

  1. This is a genuine rearrangement: the odd reciprocals 12k−1\frac{1}{2k-1}2k−11​ and the even reciprocals 12k\frac{1}{2k}2k1​ each appear exactly once, in order. Let T3NT_{3N}T3N​ be the sum of the first 3N3N3N terms; the positive terms used are the first 2N2N2N odd reciprocals and the negative terms the first NNN even reciprocals, so T3N=∑k=12N12k−1−∑k=1N12kT_{3N} = \sum_{k=1}^{2N}\frac{1}{2k-1}-\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{1}{2k}T3N​=∑k=12N​2k−11​−∑k=1N​2k1​.

  2. Since ∑k=12N12k−1=H4N−∑k=12N12k=H4N−12H2N\sum_{k=1}^{2N}\frac{1}{2k-1} = H_{4N}-\sum_{k=1}^{2N}\frac{1}{2k} = H_{4N}-\frac{1}{2}H_{2N}∑k=12N​2k−11​=H4N​−∑k=12N​2k1​=H4N​−21​H2N​, we get T3N=H4N−12H2N−12HNT_{3N} = H_{4N}-\frac{1}{2}H_{2N}-\frac{1}{2}H_NT3N​=H4N​−21​H2N​−21​HN​.

  3. Substituting Hm=ln⁡m+γ+εmH_m = \ln m+\gamma+\varepsilon_mHm​=lnm+γ+εm​ (εm→0\varepsilon_m \to 0εm​→0) gives T3N=ln⁡(4N)−12ln⁡(2N)−12ln⁡N+γ(1−12−12)+o(1)T_{3N} = \ln(4N)-\frac{1}{2}\ln(2N)-\frac{1}{2}\ln N+\gamma\left(1-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right)+o(1)T3N​=ln(4N)−21​ln(2N)−21​lnN+γ(1−21​−21​)+o(1). The γ\gammaγ terms cancel and the logarithms give ln⁡4−12ln⁡2=32ln⁡2\ln 4-\frac{1}{2}\ln 2 = \frac{3}{2}\ln 2ln4−21​ln2=23​ln2, so T3N→32ln⁡2T_{3N} \to \frac{3}{2}\ln 2T3N​→23​ln2.

  4. The intermediate partial sums follow: T3N+1=T3N+14N+1T_{3N+1} = T_{3N}+\frac{1}{4N+1}T3N+1​=T3N​+4N+11​ and T3N+2=T3N+1+14N+3T_{3N+2} = T_{3N+1}+\frac{1}{4N+3}T3N+2​=T3N+1​+4N+31​, and the added terms tend to 000, so the whole sequence TmT_mTm​ converges to 32ln⁡2\frac{3}{2}\ln 223​ln2. A conditionally convergent series can change its sum under rearrangement.
